name: Gateway of India
shortDescription: 1924 Indo-Saracenic arch on the harbour; departure point for Elephanta ferries. Best early morning before crowds.

name: Elephanta Caves
shortDescription: UNESCO rock-cut Shiva caves on an island. Coordinates are the ferry jetty at Gateway of India; duration includes ~1h ferry each way. ~120 steps up to the caves. Last ferries leave Gateway early afternoon. Price ≈ ferry return + ASI ticket.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
shortDescription: UNESCO-listed Victorian Gothic railway station, still Mumbai's busiest. Exterior viewable any time; heritage gallery tours run on weekday afternoons. Floodlit at night.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya
shortDescription: Mumbai's main museum (former Prince of Wales Museum): Indus Valley finds, miniature paintings and sculpture in a domed Indo-Saracenic building. Good heat/rain escape.

name: Marine Drive
shortDescription: 3.6 km seafront promenade, the 'Queen's Necklace' after dark. Sit on the sea wall at sunset; Girgaon Chowpatty at the north end.

name: Kala Ghoda Art District

variants.name: Kala Ghoda – short loop (Jehangir Art Gallery & a café)

shortDescription: Compact heritage precinct of galleries (Jehangir Art Gallery), Rhythm House, David Sassoon Library and cafes.

name: Fort Heritage Precinct Walk

variants.name: Fort precinct – short loop (Flora Fountain, Horniman Circle)

shortDescription: UNESCO Victorian Gothic & Art Deco ensemble: Flora Fountain, Horniman Circle, Bombay High Court and Rajabai Clock Tower (exteriors), Asiatic Society steps. Flat, pavement walk.

name: Colaba Causeway Market

variants.name: Colaba Causeway – short stroll (one stretch of stalls)

shortDescription: Street stalls for clothes, jewellery and souvenirs; bargain hard. Leopold Cafe is on this stretch.

name: Crawford Market (Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Mandai)
shortDescription: 1869 market hall with Lockwood Kipling friezes; fruit, spices and dry goods. Gateway to the Kalbadevi bazaars.

name: Banganga Tank
shortDescription: Ancient temple tank on Malabar Hill ringed by shrines and old houses; a quiet surprise in the city.

name: Haji Ali Dargah
shortDescription: 15th-century mosque and shrine reached by a 500 m causeway that floods at high tide — check tide times. Modest dress; head covering inside.

name: Shree Siddhivinayak Temple
shortDescription: Mumbai's most-visited Ganesh temple in Prabhadevi. Tuesdays and festival days bring very long queues; phones/bags restricted.

name: Mahalaxmi Dhobi Ghat
shortDescription: Open-air laundry with hundreds of washing pens, best seen from the Mahalaxmi station bridge. Guided walks go inside.

name: Worli Sea Face
shortDescription: Seafront promenade with views of the Bandra–Worli Sea Link; less crowded than Marine Drive.

name: Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Museum
shortDescription: Mumbai's oldest museum (1872) in Byculla's Jijamata Udyan; ornate Victorian interior and city history dioramas.

name: Nehru Science Centre
shortDescription: Hands-on science museum with an outdoor science park; a strong rainy-day or kids option.

name: Bandstand Promenade & Bandra Fort
shortDescription: Seafront walk past film-star homes to the 1640 Portuguese Castella de Aguada ruins; classic sunset spot.

name: Mount Mary Basilica
shortDescription: Hilltop neo-Gothic basilica; large fair in September after Mary's birthday.

name: Ranwar Village & Chapel Road Murals
shortDescription: East-Indian Catholic village lanes with painted bungalows and Bollywood street murals; pair with cafes on Hill Road.

name: Juhu Beach
shortDescription: Busy city beach — not for swimming — known for evening street food (pav bhaji, gola) and sunsets.

name: ISKCON Temple Juhu
shortDescription: Marble Radha-Krishna temple with evening aarti and kirtan; pure-veg restaurant on site.

name: Kanheri Caves (Sanjay Gandhi National Park)
shortDescription: 100+ Buddhist rock-cut caves inside a forest national park in the northern suburbs. Park entry + cave ticket; 7 km inside the park by bus/cab.

name: Shaniwar Wada
shortDescription: 1732 seat of the Peshwas; massive gates and ramparts survive after an 1828 fire. Evening light-and-sound show (separate ticket).

name: Aga Khan Palace
shortDescription: Italianate palace where Gandhi, Kasturba and Mahadev Desai were interned in 1942–44; memorials and a small museum in wide lawns.

name: Shrimant Dagdusheth Halwai Ganpati Temple
shortDescription: Pune's most famous Ganesh temple with a gold-adorned idol; spectacular during Ganeshotsav. Queues on Tuesdays and festivals.

name: Sinhagad Fort
shortDescription: Hill fort 35 km south-west, scene of Tanaji's 1670 battle. Road reaches near the top, then uneven uphill paths. Famous for pithla-bhakri and kanda bhaji stalls.

name: Raja Dinkar Kelkar Museum
shortDescription: One man's collection of 20,000+ everyday objects: lamps, nutcrackers, musical instruments, a reconstructed Mastani Mahal.

name: Pataleshwar Cave Temple
shortDescription: 8th-century rock-cut Shiva temple in the middle of the city on Jangli Maharaj Road; a quick, calm stop.

name: Parvati Hill Temples
shortDescription: Peshwa-era temple complex atop a hill, reached by ~100 stone steps; panoramic city view at sunrise.

name: Saras Baug & Talyatla Ganpati
shortDescription: Garden with an island Ganesh temple; lively evening hangout with snack stalls at the gate.

name: Vishrambaug Wada
shortDescription: Early-1800s Peshwa mansion with a carved teak facade and a small Pune history gallery.

name: Lal Mahal
shortDescription: Reconstruction of Shivaji's childhood home, next to Shaniwar Wada.

name: Tulshibaug & Laxmi Road Markets
shortDescription: Dense old-city bazaars for brassware, sarees, Paithani and daily goods. Very crowded before festivals.

name: FC Road
shortDescription: Fergusson College Road: student buzz, street shopping and iconic eateries like Vaishali.

name: Osho Teerth Park
shortDescription: Shaded Japanese-style garden with a stream and bamboo groves; restricted morning and evening hours.

name: Pu La Deshpande (Okayama Friendship) Garden
shortDescription: Japanese garden modelled on Okayama's Korakuen, built as a sister-city gift.

name: Rajiv Gandhi Zoological Park (Katraj)
shortDescription: Large zoo and snake park on the southern edge of the city; battery cars available.

name: Khadakwasla Dam
shortDescription: Reservoir on the Sinhagad road; popular for sunset and roadside corn/bhaji. Combine with Sinhagad.

name: Chaturshringi Temple
shortDescription: Hillside Devi temple up ~100 steps; big Navratri fair.

name: MG Road & Camp Bazaar
shortDescription: Cantonment high street: old bakeries (Kayani), Irani cafes, Fashion Street stalls.

name: Karla Caves & Ekvira Temple
shortDescription: 1st-century BCE Buddhist chaitya hall, one of the largest rock-cut prayer halls in India. ~350 steps up; Ekvira Devi temple at the top draws weekend crowds.

name: Bhaja Caves
shortDescription: 22 early Buddhist caves with stupas and some of the oldest reliefs in the Deccan; steep steps up from Bhaje village. Monsoon waterfall alongside.

name: Lohagad Fort
shortDescription: Maratha hill fort with the long 'Vinchu Kata' (scorpion tail) ridge. From Gaimukh Khind it's a climb of several hundred steps through four gates; slippery in monsoon.

name: Visapur Fort
shortDescription: Larger, wilder twin of Lohagad; monsoon trek up a waterfall-staircase route. For fit trekkers only.

name: Tiger's Point (Tiger's Leap)
shortDescription: Cliff edge with a ~650 m drop into the valley; clouds and waterfalls in monsoon, clear sunsets in winter. Road access; bhutta and chai stalls.

name: Lion's Point
shortDescription: Roadside valley viewpoint on the Aamby Valley road; pairs with Tiger's Point.

name: Bhushi Dam
shortDescription: Monsoon overflow cascading down wide dam steps where visitors sit in the water. Very crowded on weekends; access can be closed after heavy rain for safety.

name: Rajmachi Fort (Shrivardhan & Manaranjan)
shortDescription: Twin-fort plateau reached by a ~15 km trail from Lonavala (or a short hike from Udhewadi via Kondivade by 4x4). Fireflies in late May–June. Full day.

name: Duke's Nose
shortDescription: Beak-shaped cliff above Khandala ghat; short but steep trek with valley views.

name: Pawna Lake
shortDescription: Reservoir ringed by Tung, Tikona and Lohagad forts; lakeside camping with bonfires is the draw (camps charge separately).

name: Della Adventure Park
shortDescription: Paid adventure park (zipline, ATVs, swings); packages vary widely — price is an entry-level estimate.

name: Sunil's Celebrity Wax Museum
shortDescription: Small wax museum of Indian personalities; a rainy-day filler for families.

name: Lonavala Chikki & Fudge Market
shortDescription: Main-road shops selling Lonavala's famous chikki (nut brittle) and fudge — Maganlal, Coopers, National.

name: Venna Lake
shortDescription: Town lake with rowing/pedal boats (separately priced), horse rides and strawberry-cream stalls on the bank.

name: Arthur's Seat
shortDescription: 'Queen of Points': sheer drop to the Savitri valley ~12 km from town, with Echo Point and Tiger Spring on the way. Often fogged in during monsoon.

name: Elephant's Head (Needle Hole) Point
shortDescription: Rock formation shaped like an elephant's trunk, with a natural hole in the cliff.

name: Wilson Point (Sunrise Point)
shortDescription: Highest point in Mahabaleshwar and the classic sunrise spot, close to the market.

name: Pratapgad Fort
shortDescription: 1656 Maratha fort 24 km west, site of Shivaji's encounter with Afzal Khan (1659). Many stone steps from the parking to the upper fort.

name: Mahabaleshwar & Panchganga Temples
shortDescription: Old Mahabaleshwar's Shiva temple and the Panchganga temple where five rivers, including the Krishna, are said to originate.

name: Mapro Garden
shortDescription: Fruit-products brand's garden at Gureghar with a food court (strawberry cream, sandwiches, pizza), tasting counter and shop. Strawberry festival around Easter.

name: Table Land, Panchgani
shortDescription: Second-longest volcanic plateau in Asia; horse carts, pony rides and Krishna valley views. Short uphill walk from parking.

name: Parsi Point
shortDescription: Roadside view over the Dhom dam backwaters on the Mahabaleshwar–Panchgani road.

name: Lingmala Waterfall
shortDescription: ~150 m cascade in forest east of town; best just after the monsoon. Uneven steps down to the lower viewpoint.

name: Kate's Point & Needle Hole
shortDescription: Views of the Dhom and Balkawadi dams and the Krishna valley; popular at sunset.

name: Mahabaleshwar Main Bazaar
shortDescription: Pedestrian-friendly market for chikki, fudge, jams, leather chappals and corn patties.

name: Tapola (Shivsagar Lake)
shortDescription: 'Mini Kashmir' backwaters of the Koyna dam, ~25 km away; boating and kayaking (separately priced).

name: Ellora Caves
shortDescription: UNESCO site of 34 Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves (6th–10th c.); Kailasa (Cave 16) is a whole temple carved top-down from one rock. ~30 km from the city. Battery buses run along the 2 km site.

name: Ajanta Caves
shortDescription: UNESCO Buddhist caves (2nd c. BCE–6th c. CE) with India's finest surviving ancient murals. ~100 km (2.5–3 h) each way; mandatory shuttle bus from Fardapur T-point. Steps between caves; dolis available.

nearbyStay.name: Fardapur (near the Ajanta T-point)
nearbyStay.note: MTDC resort and small hotels ~5 km from the caves; turns a ~5h round trip into a 15-min hop and allows an early, cool, uncrowded visit.

name: Bibi Ka Maqbara
shortDescription: 1660s mausoleum of Aurangzeb's wife, modelled on the Taj Mahal ('Taj of the Deccan'). Lovely at golden hour.

name: Daulatabad Fort
shortDescription: Hilltop citadel (Devagiri) with a moat, pitch-dark tunnel passage and Chand Minar; on the Ellora road. Several hundred steep steps to the summit — carry a torch.

name: Panchakki (Water Mill)
shortDescription: 17th-century water mill powered by an underground channel, beside the dargah of Baba Shah Musafir.

name: Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga Temple
shortDescription: One of the 12 Jyotirlinga Shiva temples, 1 km from Ellora; 18th-century red-stone shikhara. Men remove shirts to enter the sanctum; long weekend/Monday queues.

name: Aurangabad Caves
shortDescription: Quiet 6th–7th century Buddhist caves on a ridge behind Bibi Ka Maqbara, with fine Tantric-Buddhist sculpture and city views.

name: Soneri Mahal
shortDescription: 17th-century Bundela palace with a small museum; venue of the Ellora-Ajanta festival.

name: Himroo & Paithani Weaving Centre
shortDescription: Workshop-showrooms demonstrating Himroo (silk-cotton brocade) and Paithani saree weaving on handlooms.

name: Gul Mandi & Old City Bazaars
shortDescription: Walled-city market lanes and gates; evening naan-qalia and kebab stalls nearby.

name: Salim Ali Lake
shortDescription: Mughal-era lake with a small bird sanctuary and boating; a calm morning stop.

name: Siddharth Garden & Zoo
shortDescription: City garden with a small zoo and snake park near the central bus stand.

name: Bhadra Maruti Temple
shortDescription: Temple with a rare reclining Hanuman idol in Khuldabad; an easy add-on to Ellora.

name: Lonar Crater Lake
shortDescription: ~50,000-year-old meteorite-impact crater with a saline lake and ruined temples on the rim, ~150 km east. Steep path down to the lake.

nearbyStay.name: Lonar town (crater rim)
nearbyStay.note: MTDC resort on the crater rim; avoids ~6h of same-day driving.

name: Paithan (Paithani Weaving Centre & Jayakwadi)
shortDescription: Ancient town ~55 km south, home of the Paithani silk saree; weaving centre, Sant Eknath samadhi, and Jayakwadi dam gardens.
